Description

POSITON SUMMARY

The Director of Development and Communications serves as a strategic leader responsible for designing, executing, and modernizing SAVE’s fundraising and marketing strategy to support our $4M annual operating budget. This role builds philanthropic partnerships, elevates organizational visibility, and leads a dedicated team. A primary mandate for this position is to assess and optimize existing internal workflows, establishing clear operational boundaries and transitioning the department toward high-performance, data-driven operations.

SUPERVISORY:
Development Associate, Grants Manager, and occasional external contractors

Essential Responsibilities

Strategic Philanthropy & Fundraising (Estimated 70%)

Strategic Planning: In partnership with the Executive Director, defines SAVE’s overarching fundraising strategies, policies, and implementation; develops a robust, multi-year development plan encompassing major gifts, annual campaigns, and corporate/foundation partnerships.
Revenue Generation: Owns accountability for meeting the organization’s annual contributed revenue goals through events, direct major donor cultivation and oversight of department initiatives.
Board Engagement: Partners with and equips the Board of Directors in fundraising activities; serves as the primary staff liaison for relevant Board committees and provides timely, data-driven progress reports.
Campaign & Relationship Management: Oversees and advances membership campaigns, individual donor pipelines, and personalized cultivation and solicitation strategies.
Grants & Institutional Giving: Directs the strategy, tracking, and reporting for all corporate, foundation, and government grant proposals, ensuring compliance and alignment with organizational goals.
Systems & Data Management: Ensures donor tracking systems (CRM) and data workflows support the business needs of the organization; assesses and implements new technology as appropriate to drive data-informed decisions.
Events: Oversees strategic donor recognition and fundraising events to maximize engagement and return on investment.

Communications & Marketing (Estimated 30%)

Brand & Messaging Strategy: Develops and executes an annual marketing and communications plan to elevate SAVE's profile across digital, print, social media, and traditional press platforms.
Hands-on Execution: Oversees and directly contributes to the creation of digital and print content, including newsletters, social media, and website updates, ensuring quality control and brand alignment.
Cross-Department Collaboration: Educates internal teams on fundraising goals and serves as the brand steward to ensure consistent messaging across all organizational programs.

Leadership, Business Process & Financial Management

Workflows: Establishes clear operational lanes, guardrails, and internal workflows to define where development activities interface with communications initiatives; optimizes the collective capacity of the team to ensure revenue-generating activities are prioritized.
Operations Optimization: Directly guides and mentors the Development Associate in elevating fundraising operations, ensuring best-in-class donor data hygiene, gift acknowledgment workflows, and stewardship touchpoints.
Team Development: Recruits, supervises, and evaluates development and communications staff and independent contractors, fostering a collaborative and high-performing culture.
Fiscal Responsibility: Collaborates with the CFO and Executive Director to construct, monitor, and manage the annual departmental budget.

Qualifications And Requirements

Minimum of 8 years of progressive development and fundraising experience in the nonprofit sector, with a proven track record of securing major gifts and corporate/foundation funding.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience in a related field. CFRE certification desired.
Change Management: Demonstrated experience in process optimization, workflow design, or scaling/rebuilding development and communications operations.
Relationship Management: Exceptional interpersonal skills with a demonstrated ability to build authentic relationships with diverse stakeholders, funders, and community partners.
Communication Skills: Superb written, oral, and presentation skills; ability to translate complex programmatic work into compelling fundraising narratives.
Technical Savvy: Proficiency with modern nonprofit CRMs/donor databases, digital fundraising platforms, and data analytics tools. Experience with agile content tools (e.g., Canva, email marketing platforms) is highly preferred.
Project Management: Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage competing deadlines, prioritize effectively, and work both independently and collaboratively.

Physical Requirements

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to walk; sit; drive; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to

stand; reach with hands and arms; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 10 pounds.

Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions except when such accommodation would cause undue hardship.

The work environment includes settings of the client’s home, educational institutions, community places, and office environments. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions except when such accommodation would cause an undue hardship.

New Mandate: Chief Operating Officer (COO)

Summary

We are a one-of-a-kind, fully-funded, and global organization dedicated to empowering philanthropic leaders everywhere to take immediate and far-reaching climate action.
By serving as an impartial guide, we equip new climate philanthropists with the information, insights, and curated roadmaps needed to drive transformative climate solutions
- our client is the climate.

We are seeking a strategic, highly capable Chief Operating Officer (COO)
to join our executive leadership team. Reporting directly to the President
, the COO will translate our 2030 strategic plan into coordinated, high-impact operations. In this pivotal role, you will lead day-to-day operations and coordinate across all key functional leaders to ensure seamless integration, operational excellence, and purpose alignment as the organization scales.

Managerial Responsibilities

The COO leads the organization's Operations, Legal, Finance, and Technology teams.
Direct Reports (5 FTE)
: Managing Director, Finance & Business Systems (Leadership Team member);Director of Operations; Interim Legal Counsel; Executive Assistant for Operations.
Indirect Reports (5.5 FTE)
: Director of Finance; Director of IT; Associate Director, Business Systems;Salesforce Administrator; Product Manager, Salesforce (0.5 FTE); Operations Coordinator.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

General Operations & Administration (40%)

Principal Operational Lead
: Oversee core administrative functions, contract management, facilities, and keyvendor relationships.
Planning & Alignment
: Lead organization-wide and cross-team priority setting and planning to removeoperational friction and foster a responsive operating environment.
Executive Strategy
: Partner with the Leadership Team on major organizational decisions affecting top-lineOKRs, strategy, and budget allocation.
Presidential Support
: Advise and support the President on operational strategies to expand and scaleengagement with key global partners.

Risk & Compliance (20%)

Legal & Risk Oversight
: Direct internal and external legal counsel to oversee risk management, regulatorycompliance, and tax/legal considerations as the organization expands.

Board Management & Funder Relations (20%)

Board Governance
: Partner with the President on the strategic management and ongoing operations of theBoard of Directors.
Funder Oversight
: Maintain governance over funder relations, including grant renewals, compliancereporting, and new funding applications.

Executive Leadership (15%)

Culture & Strategy
: Model organizational values and collaborate with the executive team to define long-termstrategic direction.
Fiduciary Responsibility
: Contribute to master budgeting and financial planning processes led by the MD ofFinance & Business Systems.
Mentorship & Coaching
: Provide leadership coaching and mentorship across teams to build an inclusive,high-performing culture.

Finance & Business Systems (5%)

Operational Integration
: Enable the success of the MD, Finance & Business Systems across financialplanning, multi-year projections, IT systems, AI integration, and Salesforce administration.

Success Criteria

Values-Driven Executive
: Models authentic, values-led leadership, balancing high-level visionary strategywith practical, hands-on execution.
Diplomatic Partner
: Navigates complex multi-partner environments with diplomatic skill, building coalitionsacross functional and organizational boundaries.
Team Architect
: Designs operational structures that break down silos, promote cross-functional innovation,and cultivate organizational resilience.
Results-Oriented Operator
: Establishes operational feedback loops that connect daily execution directly tolong-term 2030 climate goals.
Functional Leader
: Synthesizes complex operational requirements into actionable organizational strategy,proactively identifying growth opportunities and removing blockers.

Qualifications

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Executive Management
: Outstanding leadership and team-building capability across operations, finance,technology, and legal functions.
Strategic & Tactical Agility
: Demonstrated ability to move effortlessly between overarching strategy andgranular, detailed tactical execution.
Contemporary Operations Toolkit
: Comprehensive knowledge of modern operational systems, tools, andpractices required to scale growing organizations.
Entrepreneurial Rigor
: Combining the intellectual dynamism required for an entrepreneurial, fast-pacedenvironment with the discipline to build sustainable long-term infrastructure.

Education and Experience

Proven executive leadership track record (COO or senior operations lead) within high-growth, matrixed, orcomplex mission-driven organizations.
Demonstrated experience managing multi-disciplinary operational teams, supporting board governance, andoverseeing organizational risk.

Work Environment

Our organization is headquartered in San Francisco, CA, with additional staff hubs in London, New York, and Washington, D.C.
This position operates in a hybrid environment and is based in our San Francisco, CA office alongside the executive leadership team.
Staff based in the San Francisco Bay Area work in the office Tuesday through Thursday each week.

Compensation & Benefits

: Highly competitive executive compensation package, expected salary range USD 375,000 -400,000. The actual salary offered will depend on various factors, including the candidate's level of directly relevant experience, core skills, and qualifications. This is a fixed compensation rate; the role does not include an annual bonus or carried interest.
Benefits

jobs.description:
Objective and Purpose:

The  objective  of this role is to lead and manage multiple  dental  practice locations, ensuring operational efficiency, financial performance, and compliance with regulatory standards. The purpose is to build and  maintain  strong relationships with partner doctors and practice leaders, drive strategic growth initiatives, mentor and develop office managers and practice leaders, and champion change management efforts to achieve organizational goals.
The assigned territory includes CT, MA, NH, VT, ME, and Upstate/Western NY encompassing approximately 14 practices, 36+ providers, and $54.5 million in annual revenue.

  Primary Responsibilities
:  
Set and execute monthly travel plans to visit direct reports and engage with partner practices.  
Build strong relationships with partner doctors, practice leaders, and team members.  
Onboard new associates through regular communication, partnering with them, and monitoring their growth.  
Attend weekly field visits, leading by example and engaging with the entire team.  
Identify focus areas: financials, human resources/recruitment, strategic initiatives, revenue cycle management and payer relations, accounts payable, procurement, and marketing.  
Influence and implement change, standardizing plans and growth initiatives.  
Communicate organizational vision, strategic initiatives, and operational changes effectively to leadership and team members, ensuring understanding, alignment, and successful implementation across all assigned locations.  
Mentor and develop Office Managers/Practice Leaders, aligning IDP plans for growth opportunities.  
Conduct regular 1:1 meetings with managers, build strong relationships with partner surgeons and associates, and provide tools with measurable goals.  
Identify growth opportunities for practices to grow organically, manage costs, and improve the bottom line.  
Engage monthly MORs, develop SMART action plans, prepare detailed plans for hotspot practices, and measure results.  
Identify operational inefficiencies and best practices to drive organic growth.  
Manage compliance issues in partnership with the compliance team, VP of Operations, and Compliance department.  
Ensure regulatory requirements and company SOPs are met.  
Focus on employee retention, engagement, and champion companywide initiatives.  
Lead the coding initiative to ensure effective implementation of recommended coding changes.  
Align MBO goals around best practices and practice optimization initiatives.  
Maintain strong communication with VP of Operations to meet goals, standardize processes, and streamline communication with other department heads.  
Concur practice approvals and escalate to VP for final approval.  
Review all bonuses and increases with VP of Operations and follow the approval process.

Requirements
:  
Minimum of 3-5 years in a leadership role within a healthcare setting, preferably in dental or medical practices.  
Proven track record in managing multiple locations and teams.  
Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Management, or a related field.  
Strong leadership and team-building skills.  
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.  
Ability to influence and drive change effectively.  
Strong organizational and time-management skills.  
Analytical and problem-solving abilities.  
Proficiency in financial management and understanding of P&L statements.  
Knowledge of regulatory requirements and compliance standards.  
Proficiency with practice management software and other relevant technology.  
Ability to travel regularly to various practice locations.  
High level of integrity and professionalism.  
Strong commitment to employee development and retention.  
Ability to handle multiple priorities and deadlines.  
Strategic thinker with a focus on continuous improvement.  
Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation.  
Willingness to work flexible hours

Work Conditions:

Must be able to meet the travel requirements  
Must be able to sit/stand for extended periods of time.  
Must be able to reach overhead as needed.  
Must be able to lift and carry up to 25 pounds as needed.  
Must be able to work in a fast-paced environment.  
Must be able to maintain attention to detail for extended periods.  
Must be able to operate standard office equipment.  
Must be able to work flexible hours, including evenings or weekends, if required.  

Benefits:

Annual bonus plan
BCBS Medical & Dental insurance Options 
VSP Vision Coverage      
Complimentary Life Insurance Policy (employee only)
Short-term & Long-Term Disability   
Pet Insurance Coverage  
401(k) plan w/match options
HSA / FSA Account Access 
Identity Theft Protection 
Legal Services Package 
Hospital/Accident/Critical Care Coverage 
Paid Time Off

Specialty1 Partners is a practice services organization committed to providing non-clinical, business support services to the nation's leading specialty dental practices. The company was founded in 2019 by four endodontists who wanted to provide unique and differentiated support to specialty dental practices. Originally focusing on support to endodontics practices (under the Endo1 brand), Specialty1 Partners quickly expanded its support to periodontics and oral surgery practices.
Since its founding, Specialty1 Partners has grown rapidly to become one of the largest private owners of specialty dental practices in the US. jobs.description:
*This is an in-office position in Glen Ellyn, IL.*

*Relocation package available*

The Organization

The Mission of Caring Network is to honor and glorify Jesus Christ, the author and creator of life, by bringing His love and compassion to abortion minded individuals and equipping them to choose life - both physical and spiritual.

The Position

The Chief Development Officer (CDO) serves as a senior leader responsible for advancing the mission of Caring Network through strategic fundraising, donor development, and stewardship. This leader integrates and oversees direct response marketing, major donor fundraising, and communications to ensure unified messaging, consistent donor engagement, and strong financial support. Rooted in Christian values, the CDO cultivates a culture of generosity and inspires partners to engage deeply with Caring Network’s vision to glorify God by making abortion unthinkable. This role oversees the VP of Development, VP of Direct Response Marketing, Director of Communications, and the Development Administrative Assistant.

Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Develop and execute a comprehensive fundraising strategy unifying direct response marketing, major donor development, and communications.
Collaborate with the President/CEO and Leadership Team to set annual and long-term fundraising goals.
Ensure all fundraising strategies align with Caring Network’s mission and Christian values.

Fundraising & Donor Engagement

Lead major gifts, planned giving, grants, and capital campaign initiatives.
Build relationships with major donors, churches, foundations, and community partners.
Lead an omni-channel direct response program across direct mail, email, and digital ads.
Ensure stewardship practices reflect gratitude, transparency, and biblical principles of generosity.

Team Management

Supervise and mentor development, marketing, and communications staff.
Promote a collaborative, mission-driven, and faith-centered team culture.
Provide training for staff and volunteers in fundraising and donor engagement best practices.

Communications & Advocacy

Oversee marketing and communications teams to craft compelling narratives.
Ensure consistent messaging across donor communications and digital channels.
Represent Caring Network at events, conferences, and church gatherings.

Financial Oversight

Monitor development-related budgets, forecasts, and performance metrics.
Report regularly to the President/CEO on fundraising progress.
Partner with Finance to reconcile development results and ensure accuracy.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred.
7–10+ years of progressive fundraising leadership experience.
Proven track record securing major gifts and managing capital campaigns.
A committed Christian who demonstrates a personal relationship with Jesus Christ as Savior and Lord and is a participant in a local church.
Agree with and be willing to uphold Caring Network’s Statements of Faith and Principle and Core Values; Humility, Mutual Respect, Sacrificial Love, Optimism, Excellence, Integrity, Mission Focus, & Perse verance.
Strong supervisory and leadership skills.
Strong understanding of biblical stewardship and Christian values.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong relationship-building, leadership, and organizational abilities.
Ability to inspire donors and communicate vision with clarity and integrity.

Salary & Benefits

Salary: $160,000 - $180,000k BOE
Generous PTO policy, including substantial vacation time and sick time
Nine (9) paid company holidays plus Christmas Break
Paid maternity leave, paternity leave
No employee cost for health, dental, and vision insurance; discounted rates for dependents
Insurance benefits begin the first day of the month following hire date

Role Overview

Voting Rights Lab, a national nonpartisan 501(c)(3), and its 501(c)(4) affiliate are fighting the state-level battles that will shape elections in 2026, 2028, and for decades to come. In 2025 alone, we stopped a wave of proof-of-citizenship mandates in red and purple states from Texas to Michigan, and produced the first-ever map of election law vulnerabilities — showing where losing candidates can exploit state laws to challenge legitimate results. Grounded in deep state-level relationships and cross-ideological credibility, we anticipate threats and deliver solutions where democracy is most at risk.

The Coalition Director serves as the primary relationship manager and strategic coordinator for a transformational multi-organization coalition focused on countering disinformation, building cross-partisan support for policy initiatives, and creating a broader, more resilient pro-democracy movement. This role manages coalition operations, mobilizes member organizations, drives recruitment and engagement, and helps shape the coalition’s external narrative and impact in order to hone and develop stronger cross-ideological organizing models for the broader pro-democracy movement. 

The ideal candidate is a skilled coalition  builder and relationship manager who can work effectively with executives and partner organizations to scale grassroots programs and expand the breadth and depth of participation and impact. This role requires strong facilitation, communication, grassroots organizing, and program management capabilities, as well as experience in building partnerships and coalition infrastructure to drive collective action.

A Note on the Advancing Liberty Coalition

The Advancing Liberty Coalition is the heart of what makes Voting Rights Lab unusual in the democracy space. It brings together organizations that don't typically share a table: center-right democracy organizations, veterans and military families, Mormon and evangelical women's organizations, disability advocates, and business leaders.  The coalition operates on the conviction that defending democratic institutions requires a big tent — and that credibility across ideological lines is a strategic asset, not a compromise. 

Candidates who are energized by cross-ideological work and comfortable engaging authentically with partners across the political spectrum will thrive here. This is not optional — it is central to the role.
We offer a collaborative and innovative work environment, competitive compensation, and opportunities for professional advancement.

Coalition Management, Member Engagement, and Organizing 

Manage, coordinate, and drive a transformational coalition of partner organizations aligned around advancing cross-ideological democracy work.
Develop organizing models and drive opportunities across the coalition that help move campaigns, support the growth of membership organizations, and build power.

Lead recruitment and onboarding of new coalition members to expand reach, grow impact, and strengthen shared organizing models.
Push the co-creation and implementation of the coalition strategy. Ideate, incubate, nurture, and iterate on shared programs with members, advocacy, and leadership teams.

Understand, monitor, and drive coalition programs in our state portfolio. Identify organizing opportunities for coalition members that grow from our core state campaigns, provide strategic advantages to our programming, and build power for members.

Represent the coalition in external meetings, convenings, and strategic partnerships.
